name: pressure-test
description: Challenge a settled position before committing to it: one-question-at-a-time interrogation, a ranked assumption register with confirm-or-kill probes, a past-tense premortem, attacker modeling from the defender's chair, and the strongest case for the side about to be dismissed

interface.shortDescription: Five ways to challenge a plan, design, or decision before you commit, none of which renders a verdict
interface.longDescription: Five skills for one job: the user holds a plan, design, decision, or position that is settled or nearly settled and wants it challenged before committing. grill-me interrogates it one question at a time until it stops changing. assumption-check lists what must be true, ranks each assumption by weight and uncertainty, and attaches the cheapest confirm-or-kill probe. premortem imagines the accidental failure in the past tense and attaches pre-mitigations and dated tripwires. red-team models the intentional adversary: entry, steps, payoff, ranked by ease times payoff. steelman builds the strongest committed case for the side the user is about to dismiss. None of the five picks a winner or renders a verdict.
defaultPrompt: What am I assuming here, and how would I check each one?
Premortem this: it is six months later and it failed. Why?
Make the strongest case for the option I am about to reject
